pamphlet_excerpts: Scientific Proof of Permanence: Gal ton was able to scientifically prove what Herschel and Faulds already suspected, that fingerprints are permanent and unique to each individual (p. 13).
Gal ton Probability Calculation: According to Gal ton's calculations, the odds of two individual fingerprints being the same were 1 in 64 billion (p. 13).
First Official Fingerprint Files: In 1891, Juan Vucetich, an Argentine police official, began the first fingerprint files based on Gal ton pattern types (p. 13).
First Criminal Fingerprint Match: In 1892, Vucetich made the first criminal fingerprint identification (p. 13).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trace Vucetich Classification Files: In 1891, Juan Vucetich, an Argentine police official, began the first fingerprint files based on Gal ton pattern types (p. 13).
Step 2 - Review First Criminal Case: In 1892, Vucetich made the first criminal fingerprint identification (p. 13).
Step 3 - Examine Henry Classification System: The classification system was based on Gal ton's observations, as revised by Sir Edward Richard Henry (p. 13).
Step 4 - Note Early American Adoption: In 1903, the New York State prison system became the first agency in the United States to regularly use fingerprints to identify criminals (p. 13).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Fingerprinting Requirement 1, why are friction ridge skin patterns useful for lifelong personal identification, and what are the three primary fingerprint pattern families classified by Sir Francis Gal ton and Sir Edward Henry?
quiz_item.question: In Fingerprinting Requirement 1, why are friction ridge skin patterns useful for lifelong personal identification, and what are the three primary fingerprint pattern families classified by Sir Francis Gal ton and Sir Edward Henry?
options: A. Friction ridge arrangements are unique to each individual (even identical twins) and remain unchanged in pattern from before birth until decomposition; the three main pattern families are loops, whorls, and arches.
B. Fingerprints change completely every seven years as a person ages; the three main pattern families are squares, triangles, and spirals.
C. Only the thumb has friction ridges while the other four fingers are smooth; patterns are classified by skin temperature and ink color.
D. Identical twins share identical fingerprints on all ten digits; the three pattern families are epidermal, dermal, and subcutaneous.
choices: A. Friction ridge arrangements are unique to each individual (even identical twins) and remain unchanged in pattern from before birth until decomposition; the three main pattern families are loops, whorls, and arches.
B. Fingerprints change completely every seven years as a person ages; the three main pattern families are squares, triangles, and spirals.
C. Only the thumb has friction ridges while the other four fingers are smooth; patterns are classified by skin temperature and ink color.
D. Identical twins share identical fingerprints on all ten digits; the three pattern families are epidermal, dermal, and subcutaneous.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Friction ridge arrangements are unique to each individual (even identical twins) and remain unchanged in pattern from before birth until decomposition; the three main pattern families are loops, whorls, and arches.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Formed in the fetal dermal papillae, friction ridge patterns are both unique to every person and permanent throughout life, categorized into loops (about 60-65%), whorls (30-35%), and arches (5%).

pamphlet_excerpts: Methods of Personal Identification: Biometrics in our Society People can identify themselves for access and for privileges in several general ways (p. 35).
Token-Based Physical Credentials: Token-based identification systems include driver's licenses and passports (p. 35).
Knowledge-Based Secret Credentials: Knowledge-based identification systems include a computer password, apersonal identification number, and security questions for password (p. 35).
Reliability of Biometric Identifiers: Because biometric identifiers are unique to individuals, biometric identification systems are more reliable than token- or knowledge-based systems (p. 35).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Evaluate Knowledge-Based Passwords: Knowledge-based identification systems include a computer password, apersonal identification number, and security questions for password (p. 35).

Step 2 - Compare Biometric Reliability Advantages: Because biometric identifiers are unique to individuals, biometric identification systems are more reliable than token- or knowledge-based systems (p. 35).
Step 3 - Define Biometric Body Measurements: Biometrics are body measurements used to identify people (p. 35).
Step 4 - Assess Facility Access Controls: These systems can enhance security of access to computer systems and their data and to buildings, laboratories, and warehouses (p. 35).

pamphlet_excerpts: Matching Friction-Ridge Details: For an identification to be made, the friction-ridge details from two impressions must match without any unexplainabledissimilarities (p. 32).
Rule Against Unexplainable Differences: Even one unexplainable difference means the fingerprints are not from the same finger (p. 32).
No Minimum Point Requirement: No minimum amount of area or minimum number of features or points is required to make an identification (p. 32).
Identifying Small Partial Prints: Often, an area as small as the tip of a pencil eraser may be identified, if the friction-ridge detail that is present is clearly represented (p. 32).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Verify Ridge Detail Quality: No minimum amount of area or minimum number of features or points is required to make an identification (p. 32).
Step 2 - Inspect Clear Partial Impressions: Often, an area as small as the tip of a pencil eraser may be identified, if the friction-ridge detail that is present is clearly represented (p. 32).
Step 3 - Review Amnesia Victim Case: From a phone booth in a southwestern city, a mancalled the police, asking for help (p. 32).
Step 4 - Trace Civil Fingerprint Identification: When the officers arrived, they found a tall, young, red-haired manwaiting for them (p. 32).

common_misconception_pair.fact: A radial loop opens and slopes toward the thumb (the radius bone side of the forearm), so its direction on a card reverses between the left hand and the right hand (p. 18).

pamphlet_excerpts: Three Basic Pattern Families: Fingerprints are classified into three basic types, loops, arches, and whorls, based on the patterns made by the ridges that cover the skin (p. 18).
Recognizing Pattern Subcategories: Learning to recognize these general patterns and their subcategories is not hard (p. 18).

Completing Pattern Identification Worksheet: Study the examples shown in this pamphlet, then complete the worksheet found on page 38 to show your counselor you can identify the three basic types (p. 18).
Classifying Your Own Prints: Also identify the pattern types of your own fingerprints (p. 18).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Complete Pattern Practice Worksheet: Study the examples shown in this pamphlet, then complete the worksheet found on page 38 to show your counselor you can identify the three basic types (p. 18).
Step 2 - Examine Your Own Fingerprints: Also identify the pattern types of your own fingerprints (p. 18).
Step 3 - Trace Loop Ridge Recurves: In the loop pattern, the ridges begin on one side of the finger, curve or turn back sharply, and end on the same side (p. 18).
Step 4 - Determine Radial or Ulnar Slope: The loop may slope or "lean" toward either the thumb or the little finger (p. 18).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do you distinguish an ulnar loop from a radial loop when examining a fingerprint on a person's hand?
quiz_item.question: How do you distinguish an ulnar loop from a radial loop when examining a fingerprint on a person's hand?
options: A. An ulnar loop has two deltas, whereas a radial loop has only one delta
B. An ulnar loop opens toward the little finger (ulna bone), whereas a radial loop opens toward the thumb (radius bone)
C. An ulnar loop forms complete concentric circles in the center, whereas a radial loop forms a flat wave
D. An ulnar loop is found only on the left hand, whereas a radial loop is found only on the right hand
choices: A. An ulnar loop has two deltas, whereas a radial loop has only one delta
B. An ulnar loop opens toward the little finger (ulna bone), whereas a radial loop opens toward the thumb (radius bone)
C. An ulnar loop forms complete concentric circles in the center, whereas a radial loop forms a flat wave
D. An ulnar loop is found only on the left hand, whereas a radial loop is found only on the right hand
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. An ulnar loop opens toward the little finger (ulna bone), whereas a radial loop opens toward the thumb (radius bone)
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Loops are named after the forearm bones: radial loops slope and open toward the thumb (radius side), while ulnar loops slope and open toward the little finger (ulna side) (p. 18).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Fingerprinting Requirement 1, why are friction ridge skin patterns useful for lifelong personal identification, and what are the three primary fingerprint pattern families classified by Sir Francis Gal ton and Sir Edward Henry?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Fingerprinting Requirement 1, why are friction ridge skin patterns useful for lifelong personal identification, and what are the three primary fingerprint pattern families classified by Sir Francis Gal ton and Sir Edward Henry?
options: A. Friction ridge arrangements are unique to each individual (even identical twins) and remain unchanged in pattern from before birth until decomposition; the three main pattern families are loops, whorls, and arches.
B. Fingerprints change completely every seven years as a person ages; the three main pattern families are squares, triangles, and spirals.
C. Only the thumb has friction ridges while the other four fingers are smooth; patterns are classified by skin temperature and ink color.
D. Identical twins share identical fingerprints on all ten digits; the three pattern families are epidermal, dermal, and subcutaneous.
choices: A. Friction ridge arrangements are unique to each individual (even identical twins) and remain unchanged in pattern from before birth until decomposition; the three main pattern families are loops, whorls, and arches.
B. Fingerprints change completely every seven years as a person ages; the three main pattern families are squares, triangles, and spirals.
C. Only the thumb has friction ridges while the other four fingers are smooth; patterns are classified by skin temperature and ink color.
D. Identical twins share identical fingerprints on all ten digits; the three pattern families are epidermal, dermal, and subcutaneous.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Friction ridge arrangements are unique to each individual (even identical twins) and remain unchanged in pattern from before birth until decomposition; the three main pattern families are loops, whorls, and arches.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Formed in the fetal dermal papillae, friction ridge patterns are both unique to every person and permanent throughout life, categorized into loops (about 60-65%), whorls (30-35%), and arches (5%).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which of the following is an example of a token-based identification system rather than a knowledge-based or biometric system?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which of the following is an example of a token-based identification system rather than a knowledge-based or biometric system?
options: A. A driver's license or passport carried by a traveler
B. A personal identification number (PIN) entered at an ATM
C. A fingerprint scanner used to unlock a laboratory door
D. A secret security question used to reset a computer password
choices: A. A driver's license or passport carried by a traveler
B. A personal identification number (PIN) entered at an ATM
C. A fingerprint scanner used to unlock a laboratory door
D. A secret security question used to reset a computer password
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. A driver's license or passport carried by a traveler
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Driver's licenses and passports are physical objects you possess, which makes them token-based identification systems, whereas PINs and security questions are knowledge-based and fingerprint scanners are biometric (p. 35).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is required for a fingerprint examiner to make a positive identification between two fingerprint impressions?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is required for a fingerprint examiner to make a positive identification between two fingerprint impressions?
options: A. At least 16 matching ridge characteristics across the entire fingertip
B. A full rolled impression showing both deltas and the complete core
C. Matching friction-ridge details in clear agreement with no unexplainable dissimilarities
D. Confirmation that both prints belong to the same general loop or whorl pattern
choices: A. At least 16 matching ridge characteristics across the entire fingertip
B. A full rolled impression showing both deltas and the complete core
C. Matching friction-ridge details in clear agreement with no unexplainable dissimilarities
D. Confirmation that both prints belong to the same general loop or whorl pattern
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Matching friction-ridge details in clear agreement with no unexplainable dissimilarities
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A positive identification requires sufficient clear friction-ridge detail in agreement without a single unexplainable dissimilarity, and there is no fixed minimum number of points required (p. 32).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why does a standard 8-by-8-inch fingerprint card include plain (flat) impressions of four fingers taken together at the bottom of the card?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why does a standard 8-by-8-inch fingerprint card include plain (flat) impressions of four fingers taken together at the bottom of the card?
options: A. To capture the full delta-to-delta width of wide whorl patterns
B. To measure the overall length of the palm and fingers for anthropometric records
C. To wipe excess ink off the fingertips before taking the rolled impressions
D. To serve as a check that the individual rolled impressions were placed in the correct sequence
choices: A. To capture the full delta-to-delta width of wide whorl patterns
B. To measure the overall length of the palm and fingers for anthropometric records
C. To wipe excess ink off the fingertips before taking the rolled impressions
D. To serve as a check that the individual rolled impressions were placed in the correct sequence
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To serve as a check that the individual rolled impressions were placed in the correct sequence
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Plain impressions taken at the bottom of the fingerprint card act as a reference check to verify that the ten individual rolled prints were recorded in the proper finger boxes (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do you distinguish an ulnar loop from a radial loop when examining a fingerprint on a person's hand?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do you distinguish an ulnar loop from a radial loop when examining a fingerprint on a person's hand?
options: A. An ulnar loop has two deltas, whereas a radial loop has only one delta
B. An ulnar loop opens toward the little finger (ulna bone), whereas a radial loop opens toward the thumb (radius bone)
C. An ulnar loop forms complete concentric circles in the center, whereas a radial loop forms a flat wave
D. An ulnar loop is found only on the left hand, whereas a radial loop is found only on the right hand
choices: A. An ulnar loop has two deltas, whereas a radial loop has only one delta
B. An ulnar loop opens toward the little finger (ulna bone), whereas a radial loop opens toward the thumb (radius bone)
C. An ulnar loop forms complete concentric circles in the center, whereas a radial loop forms a flat wave
D. An ulnar loop is found only on the left hand, whereas a radial loop is found only on the right hand
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. An ulnar loop opens toward the little finger (ulna bone), whereas a radial loop opens toward the thumb (radius bone)
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Loops are named after the forearm bones: radial loops slope and open toward the thumb (radius side), while ulnar loops slope and open toward the little finger (ulna side) (p. 18).
